text.p: ABT Global Pharmaceutical Corp expects to begin reporting "substantial" revenues in fiscal 1998, beginning next March, President and Chief Executive Officer Elliot Friedman told Reuters.
"We're expecting revenues next year in the $14 million range," he said. "The revenues will come from licensing our technology. We're talking to a number of companies in Europe."

ABT Global, a development-stage company which intends to manufacture pharmaceutical versions of natural medicines, is also trying to license its patented "pharmaprint" technology that locates medicinal ingredients in plants.

While the market for herbal drugs extracted from plants is already a multi-billion dollar business, Friedman said drug companies still have not tapped a lot of the active ingredients in plants because they are unable to isolate and identify them. This is especially true in cases in which the active ingredient is not a single molecule, but a combination of two or more.

The Pharmaprint technology, he said, works like a fingerprinting device to locate the active ingredient, determine the compenents it includes and precisely measure them, so that it can be replicated with precision.
"With our technology, we are expecting to sharply increase the market size of pharmaceuticals derived from plants," Friedman added. "There are probably 500 (such drug candidates) out there."

One early success of the technology is a pharmaceutical version of mistletoe for which ABT Global has obtained a patent. The company is currently seeking approval for the compound, T4GEN, in Thailand and plans to conduct clinical trials aimed at U.S. approval next year.
"We are also expecting some revenues from our HIV drug in Thailand in (fiscal) 1998, but we are not putting that into our sales forecast," said Friedman.
He said the company's burn rate has been fairly consistent at about $500,000 a month, and "we expect to keep it about there until we start bringing in serious revenues."
